hypotheses.name: Verification-aware model routing
hypotheses.mechanism: Weight measured verifier quality and model health for review tasks.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare verifier-task selection under competing builder and verifier profiles.
hypotheses.kill: Routing remains unchanged or selects unavailable model.

hypotheses.name: Task risk-adjusted autonomy
hypotheses.mechanism: Derive autonomy from risk, effect, idempotency, reversibility, evidence, and human authority.
hypotheses.benefit: Increase safe autonomy for reads while constraining dangerous effects.
hypotheses.experiment: Challenge dry-run writes, external effects, low-risk reads, and prompt-derived authority.
hypotheses.success: Unsafe cases deny or require human control; bounded reads remain autonomous.
hypotheses.kill: Any prompt-derived authority or dry-run side effect is permitted.

hypotheses.name: Evidence-weighted agent planning
hypotheses.mechanism: Prefer plans whose steps declare evidence and verification outputs.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare completion correctness on equal-length plans with and without evidence requirements.
hypotheses.success: Higher verified-task rate without excessive latency.
hypotheses.kill: More ceremony without higher verification rate.

hypotheses.name: Counterfactual recovery simulation
hypotheses.mechanism: Simulate failure at each checkpoint before approving a high-risk workflow.
hypotheses.failureMode: Simulation model may omit real side effects.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare predicted recovery action with injected-failure outcomes.
hypotheses.success: No unsafe-retry mismatch across the selected matrix.
hypotheses.kill: Predictions diverge materially from injected outcomes.

hypotheses.name: Memory confidence decay
hypotheses.mechanism: Reduce authority as evidence ages or conflicts accumulate.
hypotheses.failureMode: Valuable stable facts may decay unnecessarily.
hypotheses.experiment: Evaluate stale and corrected memories over simulated time.
hypotheses.success: Lower contradiction rate without unacceptable recall loss.

hypotheses.name: Reconciliation-first tool protocol
hypotheses.mechanism: Persist intent before ambiguous external effects and require resolver-specific reconciliation.
hypotheses.benefit: Avoid blind retries after uncertain outcomes.
hypotheses.failureMode: Many tools cannot query effect status.
hypotheses.experiment: Inject timeout after remote acceptance and compare retry behavior.
hypotheses.success: No duplicate effect and explicit operator action when status is unknowable.

hypotheses.name: Adaptive context knapsack
hypotheses.mechanism: Optimize context under token budget while reserving mandatory policy and evidence slots.
hypotheses.experiment: Ablate fixed, semantic, and governed adaptive context.
hypotheses.success: Equal or better correctness with lower token cost and unsafe selection.
hypotheses.kill: Correctness falls or policy context is displaced.

hypotheses.name: Signed verifier worker
hypotheses.mechanism: Execute tests in a clean checkout and sign hashes with an independent service identity.
hypotheses.failureMode: Signing infrastructure becomes a privileged bottleneck.
hypotheses.success: Mismatched hashes are rejected and signatures verify offline.
hypotheses.kill: Service can attest mutable or unexecuted evidence.

hypotheses.name: Energy-aware local-first routing
hypotheses.mechanism: Include measured energy and idle cost in the routing Pareto frontier.
hypotheses.failureMode: Energy estimates may be too coarse.
hypotheses.experiment: Measure fixed local workloads on representative hardware.
hypotheses.success: Lower energy per verified task without quality regression.

hypotheses.name: Operator uncertainty visualization
hypotheses.mechanism: Represent evidence gaps, unknowns, and reconciliation as first-class visual states.
hypotheses.benefit: Reduce false confidence and unsafe retries.
hypotheses.failureMode: Additional signals may increase cognitive load.
hypotheses.experiment: Timed walkthrough comparing status-only and evidence-control interfaces.
hypotheses.success: Faster correct identification of next safe action.
hypotheses.kill: No comprehension gain or higher operator error.

decision: BH-001 and BH-002 were selected because they were low-cost, directly testable, reversible, and closed control gaps in active code. BH-008 was not selected because clean independent execution and signing infrastructure are unavailable in the current environment.
